title: Wildcard Parentheses Check
statement:
Decide whether a string of `(`, `)` and `*` can be read as a correctly nested set of parentheses when every `*` is free to act as `(`, as `)`, or as nothing.

Contract
- `pattern` is non-null and contains only the characters `(`, `)` and `*`; it may be empty.
- A reading is correct when every `)` closes an earlier unclosed `(` and no `(` is left open at the end.
- Each `*` may be chosen independently as `(`, `)` or an empty string. Return true if at least one choice gives a correct reading.
- An empty `pattern` is correct.

Examples
- `isBalanced("(*))")` is true: read the star as `(` to get `(())`.
- `isBalanced("*(")` is false: the final `(` can never be closed.
- `isBalanced("")` is true.
hints: If there were no stars, a single counter of open parentheses would be enough. With stars the count of open parentheses becomes a range.
Track the lowest and highest possible number of open parentheses: `(` raises both, `)` lowers both, and `*` lowers the low end and raises the high end. Never let the low end drop below zero.
If the high end ever goes negative there are too many `)`; at the end the low end must be zero. Intended complexity: O(n) time for a string of length n and O(1) extra space.
inputSyntax: Input: a string of ( ) and * characters, for example: (*))
